problem.name: Two-dimensional hidden linear function
problem.statement_latex: On an $n$-vertex square grid, input bits $A_e,b_v$ define $q(x)=2\sum_{e=\{u,v\}}A_ex_ux_v+\sum_v b_vx_v\pmod4$. Let $L_q=\{x:q(x\oplus y)=q(x)+q(y)\ \forall y\}$. Output $z\in\mathbb F_2^n$ with $q(x)=2z^Tx$ for every $x\in L_q$. Complexity counts bounded-fan-in circuit depth.

quantum.headline_latex: $O(1)$ depth and $O(n)$ gates on a nearest-neighbor grid: apply $H^{\otimes n}$, the Clifford phase $i^{q(x)}$, and $H^{\otimes n}$. Every measured output satisfies the relation. An encoded construction extends the separation to a related noisy three-dimensional task.

classical.headline_latex: $\Omega(\log n)$ depth for bounded-fan-in randomized classical circuits solving all instances with the stipulated success probability. Stabilizer simulation or finite-field linear algebra gives polynomial sequential time; parallel linear algebra gives polylogarithmic depth.
